Header: Candidatus Phytoplasma palmae Coconut lethal yellowing disease

Prevention: Coconut lethal yellowing disease is caused by a phytoplasma (‘bacteria like’ organism), spread by a planthopper ( Haplaxius crudus ).
Replace grass ground cover with legumes or other non-grass cover to reduce planthopper population.
Young planthoppers live in the root zone of grassy plants.
Lignum vitae ) to reduce wind-aided movement of planthoppers.
Implement strict on-farm quarantine by reducing human movement of infected palms and alternate hosts for the disease, such as grasses.
Ensure good fertilization programmes (informed from soil nutrient test) for strong palm stands.
Monitoring: Lethal yellowing disease cannot be properly identified by symptoms alone as other diseases; including mineral deficiencies may show similar symptoms.
Implement strict weekly surveillance 3 months after field establishment as symptoms will not appear immediately after infection.
Yellowing of older leaves moving upwards to the crown to younger leaves which die within 6 months after first symptoms are seen.
Yellowed leaves which soon turn brown, dry out and hang down to form a skirt around the trunk for several weeks before falling.
Direct Control: Promptly remove infected plants, and burn.
Restrictions: Plant hoppers can easily be moved with the wind and so chemical treatment of this disease vector is not considered effective.
Phytoplasma diseases cannot be treated with pesticides
